In the Targums with Patah אַדְרַע .
Hence
אֶדְרֶעִי (strong, mighty) Edrei, pr. n.
a) The former metropolis of Bashan,
situated in the territory of Manasseh,
Called by Eusebius Ἀδραά, by Ptolemy
with עָגַב, ἀγαπάω. With acc. Gen. 37,
3. 4. Deut. 4, 37 ; rarely c. לְ Lev. 19, 18.
17 אַהֲבַת נַפְשׁוֹ אֲהֵבוֹ he loved him as he
loved his own soul. Part. אֹהֵב a friend,
loving and beloved, intimate, different
from רֵעַ a companion, Prov. 18, 24. Esth.
5, 10. 14. Is. 41, 8 זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי the
seed of Abraham my friend.
3. to love to do any thing, to delight
in doing, seq. infin. c. לְ , Hos. 12, 8 לַעֲשֹׁק
אָהֵב he loveth to oppress. Is. 56, 10. Jer.
Niph. part. נֶאֱהָב lovely, amiable, wor-
Ἄδρα, by Arabian geographers زرع
Zer'a, now درعا Der'â. [According to
Euseb. and the Peut. Tables, it lay 24
Rom. miles from Bozrah on the way to
Capitolias and Gadara. See Reland
Palæstina p. 547. Bibl. Res. in Pal. III.
App. p. 152.—R.] b) A city in Naph-
tali, Josh. 19, 37.
אַדֶּרֶת 1. Fem. of adj. אַדִּיר, large,
great, mighty, (comp. שַׁלִּיט, f. שַׁלֶּטֶת,)
Ez. 17, 8 גֶּפֶן אַדֶּרֶת a large vine, i. e. full
of branches and leaves. Comp. אַדִּיר
no. 1.
thy of love, 2 Sam. 1, 23.
Piel part. מְאַהֵב 1. a friend, Zech.
2. a lover, but only in a bad sense, a
paramour, debauchee, Ez. 16, 33 sq. 23,
5 sq. i. e. metaph. for an idolater.
Deriv. the three following.
אֹהַב, only in plur. אֳהָבִים 1. loves,
spec. in a bad sense, amours, trop. of
intercourse and alliances with foreign
nations, Hos. 8, 9.
2. delight, loveliness. Prov. 5, 19 אַיֶּלֶת
אֲהָבִים a lovely hind.
2. Subst. a wide cloak, mantle, pallium,
אַדֶּרֶת שִׁנְעָר a Babylonish mantle Josh. 7,
21, i. e. variegated with figures, having
the figures of men and animals interwo-
ven in colours; comp. Plin. H. N. 8. 48.
So אַדֶּרֶת שֵׂעָר a hairy mantle, shaggy
with hair, or (according to some) of fur,
3. splendour, glory, Zech. 11, 3.
* אָדַשׁ i. q. דּוּשׁ, to thresh, once inf.
absol. Is. 28, 28 אָדוֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁנּוּ threshing
he threshes it.
* אָהֵב and אָהַב fut. יֶאֱהַב and יֶאֱהָב,
אֹהַב m. love, in sing. once meton. for
lovers, paramours, Hos. 9, 10. Sept.
οἱ ἠγαπημένοι. Plur. אֳהָבִים loves, spec.
amours, Prov. 7, 18.
אַהֲבָה f. 1. Inf. fem. of the verb אָהַב,
with לְ pref. Is. 56, 6 לְאַהֲבָה אֶת־שֵׁם יְהוָֹה
to love the name of Jehovah. Deut. 10,
בְּ 1 K. 10, 9 בְּאַהֲבַת יְהוָֹה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל in
Jehovah's loving Israel, i. e. because he
loved Israel. In the same sense with
pref. כְּ Hos. 3, 1, and מִן Deut. 7, 8 מֵאַהֲבַת
יְהוָֹה אֶתְכֶם because Jehovah loved you.
2. love, espec. between the sexes, Cant.
2, 4. 5, 8. 8, 6. 7; of God towards men
1 pers. אֵהָב Prov. 8, 17 and אֹהַב Hos. 14,
5 ; inf. אֱהֹב Ecc. 3, 8, also אַהֲבָה q. v.
1. to breathe after, to long for, to de-
כִּי Ps. 116, 1.—This sense of breathing
after belongs to the syllables הב, חב,
and with the letters softened אב, או ;
comp. the roots חָבַל ; חָבַב, حَبَّ to de-
sire, to love ; אָוָה and אָבָה to desire, to
be willing.
2. to love, in which signif. it is kindr.
Hos. 3, 1 ; of friends towards each other,
3. love, delight, concr. one beloved,
fem. Cant. 2, 7. 3, 5. So perh. v. 10,
where others as adv. lovely.
* אָהַד obsol. root, i. q. אָחַד to be one,
united. Hence אֵהוּד and
אֹהַד Ohad, pr. n. of a son of Simeon,
* אֲהָהּ interj. expressing grief, sor-
